post_topic: Why LLM-agnostic design with HITL governance isn't optional for production AI systems — it's the only architecture that survives contact with the enterprise
scene_description: A split architectural diagram contrasting two system designs side by side: on the left, a fragile 'demo-architected' stack where the LLM (labeled GPT-4o, Claude 3.5, or Gemini Ultra) sits directly in the business logic with pending HITL states stored in a cache with a TTL that can be evicted; on the right, the Cloud Decoded production architecture showing the LLM sitting behind an abstraction interface, HITL checkpoints implemented as a durable-execution state machine that survives restarts and deployments, and multi-tenant isolation enforced at the infrastructure layer. The left side is marked with warning indicators showing cache eviction killing human review, while the right side shows a logged rejection reason feeding back into the prompt context, illustrating the difference between a system architected for a demo and one built for a compliance officer.
